overhang.note: Most FDM printers handle up to 45° without support. Printer and material dependent.

bridging.note: Depends heavily on material, speed, and cooling. PLA typically bridges better than PETG.
bridging.recommendation: Keep bridges short. Add supports for spans > 10mm if quality critical.

wall_thickness.rule_of_thumb: Minimum wall = nozzle_diameter * 2 for structural, nozzle_diameter * 1 absolute minimum
wall_thickness.recommendation: Use multiples of line width for best results

layer_adhesion.note: FDM parts are weakest between layers (Z direction). Design critical load paths along XY.
layer_adhesion.anisotropy: Z-axis strength typically 50-75% of XY strength

tolerances.note: NEEDS_INPUT from printer calibration. Typical FDM: ±0.2mm

orientation.principle: Orient for strength, minimum support, and best surface quality
rules: Largest flat surface on bed for stability
Critical dimensions in XY plane where possible
Load direction along layer lines, not across

bed_adhesion.brim_when: Small contact area, tall parts, ABS/Nylon

snap_fit.deflection_note: FDM layer orientation affects flex behavior. Print arms along their length.
snap_fit.stress_concentration: Add fillets at base of snap arms to reduce stress concentration

holes.minimum_diameter_mm: Depends on nozzle. Generally 2x nozzle diameter minimum.
holes.horizontal_holes: Use teardrop shape for better bridging on top
holes.vertical_holes: More accurate than horizontal. Prefer vertical orientation.

_provenance.note: Typical FDM values (e.g. 45 deg overhang) are guidelines, never printer capabilities. No consumer may promote them to slicer parameters.
